findings.title: Eight of the ten LS-DATA-009 chunk exceptions are an extraction-rule artifact
findings.detail: Each chunk block begins with its own metadata lines ('Chunk characters: …', 'Chunk SHA-256: …'). An extractor that takes everything between BEGIN and END swallows those lines, which is why the audit recorded 'Only base64 data is allowed'. Skipping the declared header lines makes eight of the ten blocks decode and reproduce their own declared chunk digests. The two that still fail (V2_CHUNK_1, V3_CHUNK_1D) are the two the carrier itself marks FAILED / DO NOT USE.
findings.consequence: A reader fix, not a mathematical result. It restores a dependency; it promotes nothing.

findings.title: The carrier-declared LS-DATA-009 result and the published reading copy are different bytes
findings.detail: Following the carrier's own reconstruction rule (V3 1A+1B+1C, V4 1D-A+1D-B, then V2 chunks 2–4) yields a 14,604-character stream whose sha256 is d097629a… — the value the carrier declares — decoding to 10,953 bytes with sha256 07e02214…, again the value the carrier declares. The document's separate unchunked BEGIN_FULL_RESULT_BASE64 block also decodes to 10,953 bytes, but to sha256 39e3defd…, and that is the variant the accessibility publication published as its 'RECOVERED CAPSULE READING COPY' (its header even notes 'Digest declared in carrier: False'). The two differ in exactly three places: the JSON key 'normalizer.conservative_c_A' (denominator of 51 digits versus 54), 'perturbation.covariance_difference_bound' (two digits absent), and one line break.
findings.consequence: Recorded as a byte-level fact for whoever adjudicates. Both variants are stored under recovery/recovered/ with their digests in their paths. This ledger does not decide which is correct, does not touch the register status of LS-DATA-009-v1.1, and does not evaluate either constant.

findings.title: A block that decodes without error is not thereby the payload its carrier declares
findings.detail: GP-DATA-114-v1.0's BEGIN_RECEIPT_GZIP_BASE64 block decodes and gunzips cleanly, so the audit raised no exception for it, but it yields 1,923 bytes from an 849-byte gzip while the carrier declares a 4,546-byte receipt (sha256 8472209e…) in a 1,149-byte gzip (sha256 1fc216aa…). The corpus's published 'decoded_payload' fe4ef5d5… is the 1,923-byte object.
findings.consequence: An identity mismatch that no error message would have surfaced. Reported, not repaired.

findings.title: The reading copies are byte-faithful for plain text and not for these Markdown payloads
findings.detail: One deterministic extraction rule (CONTENT block, CRLF→LF, strip trailing newlines, append one LF) reproduces the declared payload digest exactly for arithmetic_ledgers.out.txt (859 B), first_variation_derivation.out.txt (370 B), SHA256SUMS (1,578 B) and the decoded LS-DATA-009 and GP-DATA-114 capsules. The same rule applied to the two .md audit payloads yields +22 and +10 bytes against their own declared counts, and no tested normalisation closes the gap.
findings.consequence: Those two are CANDIDATEs, not recoveries, and are stored as such.

findings.title: The eight empty capsules were created empty, not emptied
findings.detail: For the three LS-DATA-015 shells Drive reports createdTime == modifiedTime (2026-07-25 22:19:38.365Z, 22:20:40.640Z, 22:21:59.144Z), i.e. no post-creation revision is recorded, and the bodies are still a bare UTF-8 BOM on fresh 2026-09-18 bytes. findings.title: The reading volumes display every blank line twice; inverting that rule turns the two Markdown candidates into corroborated recoveries
findings.detail: A payload whose bytes were independently in hand (the LS-DATA-013 verifier, extracted from its carrier zip) was compared with its reading copy: every run of k consecutive newlines in the payload is displayed as 2k-1 newlines, i.e. every blank line is shown twice.
